chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal remedy instructs the user to run `ddflow complete {named} --regression-test`. This is an incomplete command: `--regression-test` requires a `<test>` argument, as the change's own intent shows (`ddflow complete fix-... --regression-test <test>`). A user who follows the suggested command literally gets a CLI argument-parsing error instead of a closable command.

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds `_merge` to the surrounding regression-verdict tests but misses the test that ends at line 127 with `assert out.data["regression_verified"] == "could-not-run", out.data`. That test is set up via `_case(repo)`, which leaves `fix-B1` unmerged. After the new fix-not-landed gate, `api.bug_fixed` with no `--landed` now returns the `fix-not-landed` refusal before the regression runner is reached, so `out.data["regression_verified"]` is not `could-not-run` and the assertion fails. Running this test after the change will fail, so the change does not pass its own test suite; the test should call `_merge(repo)` before `api.bug_fixed` like the adjacent tests.

data.claim: A same-family-as-author reviewer's finding (family==author family) holds a review gate open even when a cross-family reviewer reviewed clean (0 findings), because _gate_outcome/_blocking_findings aggregate every heard reviewer's finding as blocking regardless of reviewer family
data.falsifier: A round where grok(xai)+gemini(google) report 0 findings and a deepseek reviewer reports 1 finding would record the gate PASSED (same-family finding discounted); if it records FAILED instead, the reduction is wrong
data.mechanism: cross-family clean is authoritative but the same-family finding is counted in _blocking_findings, so the gate records failed and failed_review_blockers refuses merge
data.question: Should a same-family-as-author reviewer's non-converging finding block the gate when a cross-family reviewer passed clean?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED research R2980e42651: root cause read from _gate_outcome/_blocking_findings (every heard reviewer's finding aggregated as blocking regardless of reviewer family); regression test tests/test_review_identifying_reviewer.py::test_a_same_family_finding_does_not_block_when_cross_family_is_clean fails on unfixed code and passes on the fix

Followed r-unavailable-not-pass (reviewer outcomes recorded honestly), r-bounded-everything (same-family discount caps non-convergence rather than indefinite refusal), r-gemini-key-load (load GEMINI_API_KEY before the cross-family review), r-task-phase-needs-wave (fix task), and D-reviewer-independence-soft (author's own family is not independent evidence). No rule forbids discounting same-family findings over a clean cross-family verdict.

chunk_findings.detail: In `_cross_family_clean`, a reviewer whose family is equal to `author_fam` is skipped (`_rev_family(r, cfg) != author_fam`), but if `_rev_family(r, cfg)` returns `""` (empty string, representing an unrecognized or unknown family), it is also incorrectly skipped by the condition `_rev_family(r, cfg) != ""`. This means that an unrecognized/unknown reviewer with no findings is treated as a valid "cross-family clean" reviewer, allowing an unknown family reviewer to discount a same-family or known-family reviewer's findings even when no verified independent cross-family reviewer has passed clean. Given an author of family "openai", an unknown reviewer (`family=""`) that returns 0 findings, and a same-family reviewer (`family="openai"`) that returns a finding, `_cross_family_clean` returns `True` because the unknown reviewer is neither empty (skipped by `!= ""`) nor matches `author_fam`, which causes the same-family finding to be incorrectly discounted and the gate to pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_cross_family_clean

chunk_findings.detail: The stated failure is a prior same-family confirmed finding with no later clean delta (`_confirmed_unrechecked`), while a cross-family reviewer is already clean. `_gate_outcome` still returns `"failed"` whenever `converged_round and _confirmed_unrechecked(it, gate)` and does that before the new `if discounted` pass. Given `converging=True`, a prior review with `chunk_findings`, `_confirmed_unrechecked` true, this round a same-family reviewer still raising findings and a cross-family `REVIEWED` result with no findings, `author_model` resolving to that same family: findings are discounted, `blocking` is empty, then the unrechecked check fails the gate anyway. The discount never runs, so B7dbf432caa stays open on a full re-review.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_gate_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: When `GD.family_name_of(author_model, cfg.agent.families)` returns `None` and `GD.router_set` returns `None`, the return expression `(bare or GD.family_of(author_model, cfg)).strip().lower() or None` calls `.strip()` on the raw result. If `GD.family_of(author_model, cfg)` returns `None` for an unrecognized name — the exact case the docstring says should produce `None`, and the case the adjacent `_rev_family` explicitly guards with `or ""` — this raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip'`. Example: `author_model="unmapped-model"` with no entry in `cfg.agent.families` or `cfg.agent.routers` and `GD.family_of` returning `None` crashes `_blocking_findings` instead of returning `None` and proceeding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_author_single_family

chunk_findings.detail: The new same-family discount is unreachable in the exact bug B7dbf432caa case. Suppose a same-family reviewer (author family) already has a prior confirmed finding recorded in `gate` and never converges, while gemini/google and grok/xai both return clean. In the full re-review, `_blocking_findings` returns `blocking=[]`, `discounted=[...]`, and `converged_round=True`. Execution then hits `if converged_round and _confirmed_unrechecked(it, gate): return "failed", extra_evidence` before the new `if discounted:` branch, so the prior same-family confirmed finding still blocks and the cross-family clean verdict cannot close the gate. The added comment explicitly says a prior confirmed finding still blocks, which is the opposite of the stated fix requirement.
